properties.description: Built 2026-10-17 in reflow2-core's inference and reasoning modules (PR on branch feat/a-proof-says-what-it-assumes-and-asks). A PREMISE_OF edge can carry `role: assumed` (add_inference's `assumed`): the premise holds inside the argument whatever its own truth, and every node resting on the step carries it as an open assumption. `Inference.discharges` (add_inference's `discharges`, refused unless something beneath the step assumes it) removes it: the conclusion's truth, its foundations (an assumption is never a foundation) and the what-if (an assumed link is not walked) read without it. A claim holding only under an undischarged assumption reads proof_status `conditional`; FoundationsReading lists `assumes`; reasoning_report lists `assumptions`, each read "assumed, discharged by <step>" or "assumed, never discharged", and an undischarged one is a `reasoning_not_as_stated` gap and counted in loop_status.reasoning. Trial shape: Euclid's reductio, "suppose the primes are finite", recorded honestly.
properties.name: A proof step takes a premise up as an assumption, and a later step discharges it: the conclusion then rests on it nowhere
